newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australia sees April lull in housing - agents.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australia sees April lull in housing - agents.

text.p: April was generally a quiet month for the Australian property market, with prices and rents rising slightly in most cities, the Real Estate Institute of Australia (REIA) said on Sunday.
Most agents reported that the number of properties listed for sale were stable or slightly down, while levels of inquiry were steady, the REIA said in a statement.
Trend median house prices rose in Sydney, Melbourne, Brisbane, Adelaide and Perth, but fell in Canberra, Hobart and Darwin.
By far the biggest rise was in Sydney, up 2.1 percent in April and up 13.9 percent over the past 12 months.
Median home prices rose 0.6 percent in April in Melbourne, 0.5 percent in Perth and 0.3 percent in Brisbane.
REIA president Don Brindley said economic uncertainty was putting a brake on the real estate market despite high levels of home loan affordability.
